You risked very light to build confidence. That's fine, but set a rule for when you go back to normal size (for example, after 3 trades like this taken by the plan), or light size becomes the new comfort zone.
'It would've been a $50 loss, not a big deal' shows the calm came from tiny size. Notice whether you feel the same at full size.

questions.answer: Overnight we rebalanced the 4hr and tapped it in London, then came all the way back down and swept the low that took PDL last night. I wanted that reset low to fail to go lower and form a protected low, flip, and long to the 1hr bullish gap. It never gave me the long entry, so I switched to the short once it pumped into the bearish leg's OTE with weak 1min candles.
questions.q: At 9:29, ES had already broken below its PD-L, AS.L and NYPM.L while NQ was only tagging PD-L. When you wrote 'take out the LRL on the 1min,' did you mean NQ running those same lows? And did you read ES breaking first as bearish strength, or as a possible bullish SMT at the lows?
questions.reply: Got it. You had two scenarios: long to the 1hr gap if a protected low formed, or short if price ran into the OTE weak. When the long trigger never came, you didn't chase it and took the setup that did show up. That's disciplined. Put both scenarios in PRE MARKET next time, because your one line ('take out the LRL... might just continue to dump') hid a really solid plan.

questions.answer: Target was internal liquidity, the EQ of the NY AM bullish leg. I'd possibly hold until ES hit the NYAM low and formed a bullish SMT, because I don't want to be in when an SMT forms against me. No major HTF draw today: weekly objective was already done (no-wick weekly candle, then the wick yesterday), so I risked light and played safe.
questions.q: You took everything off at the bullish leg's EQ (~29,093), with D OPEN just above and NYAM.L (~28,995) below. What's your rule for full exit at the EQ vs leaving a runner toward the NYAM low?
questions.reply: Your exit rule is clear and it worked: right after your TP, ES swept the NYAM low, bullish SMT formed, and price pumped. Exiting at the EQ was the safe internal target, and 'out when an SMT forms against me' is a real rule. Write it in your model so you use it every time. Sizing down because there's no major draw is also the right instinct. Most traders do the opposite on slow Fridays.

questions.answer: Stop always goes at a protected high (or protected low for longs). I waited past 10:00 because I don't enter 5 minutes before the 10am 4hr open, to avoid getting manipulated. After 10 we failed to take the high twice, 5min rejection block, double bearish SMT, and the 1hr bearish gap was already mitigated.
questions.q: What made this trade feel different from Oct 22, when you faded the 5min IFVG and missed the move? What did you see today that you didn't wait for yesterday?
questions.reply: That's the difference from Oct 22: today you had a time rule (nothing just before the 10am 4hr open) and waited for confirmation that the high had failed twice, so the entry came after the manipulation instead of during it. On Oct 22 AB said the 9:30 accumulation set up the 10am move. Today you respected that timing.
